meta.title: Eye-movement analysis from the EOG: finding REM sleep
meta.tools: Horizontal EOG, derivative-based saccade detection, per-stage rate statistics; Sleep-EDF Expanded
meta.summary: Detect rapid eye movements in a whole night of horizontal EOG with a velocity-threshold detector and show that they concentrate in REM sleep and wakefulness, as the name 'REM' says — then use the rate alone to spot REM epochs.
meta.problem: The electrooculogram measures the eye's corneo-retinal dipole. Can eye movements alone reveal dream sleep?
meta.theory:
Horizontal eye rotation changes the EOG by roughly 10–20 µV per degree; saccades are fast (velocity ≫ slow drifts), so a threshold on |dV/dt| detects them.
REM sleep is defined by bursts of such movements; N2/N3 contain almost none (slow rolling movements occur mainly in N1). Expected: REM-epoch saccade
rate ≫ N2/N3 rate, making the rate a useful REM indicator (but also high during wake).
meta.method:
SC4001 night: EOG horizontal (100 Hz), 0.3–15 Hz band-pass, velocity = derivative smoothed over 30 ms, saccade = |velocity| > 6 × MAD with 200 ms refractory period. Rate per
30-s epoch grouped by the expert's stage; REM detection by rate threshold restricted to sleep epochs (ROC area).

rows.quantity: REM / N2 mean saccade-rate ratio (≫ 1 expected)
ROC area for REM vs other sleep epochs from saccade rate alone

metrics.quantity: Detection threshold (6 × robust σ of velocity)
